title: Step Supporting Error Handling Unit Lifecycle Contract

scope.purpose: Define lifecycle responsibilities and boundaries for Error Handling Unit instances, including provisioning, preparation, readiness, admission, invocation eligibility, quiescence, reuse, release, and independent retention of operation results.
scope.appliesTo: Each concrete Step specialization that provisions, acquires, admits, reuses, or releases Error Handling Unit instances.

separation: Unit instance lifetime is distinct from each Association lifetime.
Unit instance lifetime is distinct from each invocation and each handling operation attempt/execution.
Unit instance lifetime is distinct from the lifetime of Publisher capabilities supplied for individual invocations.
Unit instance lifetime is distinct from the retention lifetime of accepted operation entries and ErrorHandlerResult aggregates.
Ending the last Association does not automatically release the Unit instance.
Retaining operation results does not require retaining the runtime Unit instance.
lifecyclePrinciples.authority: Step Composition owns lifecycle decisions and coordinates lifecycle transitions. The concrete Unit implementation performs its own initialization, operation-specific preparation, shutdown, and resource-release mechanics.
lifecyclePrinciples.specialization: The common contract defines obligations and conceptual milestones only; it does not impose one universal state machine, pool, factory, scheduler, or resource-management implementation.

lifecycleMilestones.name: ProvisionedOrAcquired
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: A Unit instance has been created or obtained and has a stable errorHandlingUnitIdentity.

lifecycleMilestones.name: Prepared
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: Specialization-required configuration, dependencies, credentials/capabilities, and operation resources have been prepared.

lifecycleMilestones.name: Ready
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: The Unit satisfies its declared technical readiness conditions.

lifecycleMilestones.name: Admitted
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: Step Composition has authorized the Unit for use within the owning Step.

lifecycleMilestones.name: AvailableOrInUse
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: The Unit is eligible for invocation or is currently executing one or more authorized invocations/operations.

lifecycleMilestones.name: Quiescing
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: Step Composition has stopped authorizing new invocations and is coordinating completion/cancellation of active work and result custody.

lifecycleMilestones.name: RetainedForReuse
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: The same runtime instance remains available for possible future use under the Step's reset, isolation, and readiness rules.

lifecycleMilestones.name: Released
lifecycleMilestones.meaning: Release has completed successfully and the instance is no longer eligible for invocation or association.

rules: Milestones are conceptual lifecycle descriptions, not a mandatory enum or linear state machine.
A specialization may omit, combine, repeat, or refine milestones.
The concrete Step defines transition ordering and conditions.
A Unit may be admitted and available without an active Association if the Step permits it.
Released means successful completion of release; failed or indeterminate release remains unresolved and must not be labelled Released.

stepComposition: Decides whether the Unit is provisioned, acquired, admitted, made available, reused, quiesced, or released.
Determines whether the Unit is eligible for new invocations and which associations may authorize them.
Coordinates association termination, invocation closure, and operation-result custody before release.
Defines reset, isolation, reuse, concurrency, and release policies for the concrete Step.
unitImplementation: Performs technical preparation and reports readiness.
Implements operation execution resource setup and shutdown where applicable.
Stops accepting new work after authorization is withdrawn.
Reports quiescence and release outcomes through the specialized lifecycle boundary.
Releases resources it owns according to the Step specialization.
associationTarget: May expose or withdraw target-specific access capabilities under its own contract.
Does not acquire lifecycle authority over the Unit merely by being an association target.
publisherAndComposition: The Step-specific Error Handling Composition owns invocation-scoped Publisher capabilities and accepted-entry retention.
Publisher lifetime and accepted-entry retention are governed by their own contracts; releasing a Unit does not release or invalidate entries already accepted by the Composition.
The Unit does not own the Publisher merely because it receives an invocation-scoped capability.

rules: Technical readiness is distinct from Step Composition admission.
An instance may be associated only under the concrete Step's lifecycle and Association preconditions.
Association establishment does not itself authorize an invocation until the Step's activation/admission conditions are satisfied.
Step Composition must authorize each invocation against a currently valid Association and eligible Unit instance.
The Unit must not accept new invocations after Step Composition withdraws authorization.
The concrete Step defines whether a Unit may serve multiple associations or concurrent invocations and what isolation is required.
Each invocation has a lifetime distinct from the Unit instance and is correlated with one selected Association.
Each operation attempt and actual operation execution has an identity and lifetime distinct from the enclosing invocation.
The concrete Step defines whether invocations are synchronous, asynchronous, concurrent, reentrant, cancellable, or serialized.
The concrete Step defines whether the Unit is stateless, stateful, reusable, single-use, or externally backed.
A completed invocation does not imply that the Unit instance must be released.
An invocation-scoped Publisher capability may be closed after its closure conditions are met; this does not close the Unit instance.

preReleaseConditions: Step Composition has stopped authorizing new invocations for the Unit.
All Associations that could authorize new invocations have been ended or rendered unusable under the Association Contract.
Active invocations, handling operations, callbacks, and asynchronous work have completed, been cancelled, or been explicitly reconciled.
Every granted PublicationReservation is Consumed or Released, or any unresolved reservation/result has been transferred to the named Recovery Owner under a verifiable custody protocol.
Every produced-but-unaccepted THandlingOperationResult remains recoverable under Unit custody or an explicitly designated Recovery Owner.
Accepted operation entries are retained by the Step-specific Error Handling Composition and remain independent of Unit lifetime.
Unit-owned target handles, access capabilities, callbacks, and operation resources have been detached or scheduled for safe release.
releaseRules: Step Composition decides when release is appropriate and coordinates the release operation.
The Unit implementation performs release mechanics for resources it owns.
Successful release is recorded only after the implementation confirms completion.
Failed or indeterminate release remains unresolved and must not be treated as successful or made eligible for reuse without reconciliation.
Release does not erase accepted operation entries, ErrorHandlerResult aggregates, or historical provenance.
Release does not require retaining the Unit runtime instance merely because historical results refer to errorHandlingUnitIdentity.

rules: Reuse is permitted only when the concrete Step allows it and the instance satisfies readiness, reset, and isolation requirements.
The Step defines whether reuse requires reconfiguration, cleanup, or revalidation of external dependencies.
The same runtime instance retains errorHandlingUnitIdentity across reuse; a replacement instance receives a new identity.
New Associations and invocations receive new identities; prior operation provenance is never reused.
Reuse must not attribute pending operations or results from a prior invocation/association to a later one.
No universal object pool, reference count, lock, or lifecycle manager is mandated.

Provisioning, preparation, readiness, invocation, operation, quiescence, and release failures are distinct lifecycle/execution facts; they are not automatically operation results or Error Occurrences.
The concrete Step defines retry, replacement, quarantine, compensation, or escalation policy.
A failed or indeterminate release must not be represented as Released.
If operation-result custody is unresolved, the Unit must not be destroyed or released in a way that loses the only recoverable representation.
A Publisher status-query failure does not prove non-acceptance; the Step's publication recovery contract governs reconciliation.
Previously accepted operation entries remain valid after later Unit failure or release.
Operation entries and their provenance may outlive the Unit instance and its Associations.
Publisher-accepted entries are retained by the Step-specific Error Handling Composition according to the Publisher and Step specialization contracts.
Recovery Owner records may outlive the Unit where custody has been explicitly transferred.
Retained result content must not depend on runtime handles or borrowed resources that are released with the Unit unless the Step explicitly preserves those resources for an independent reason.
Historical errorHandlingUnitIdentity, errorHandlingUnitAssociationIdentity, and invocation/operation identities remain interpretable after release.
Retention policy and ownership of ErrorHandlerResult are defined by the Step-specific Error Handling Composition and result contracts, not by the Unit's runtime lifetime.

required: Define provisioning/acquisition and identity assignment for errorHandlingUnitIdentity.
Define preparation and technical readiness criteria.
Define admission, association eligibility, and invocation authorization conditions.
Define the lifetime of Unit instances, invocations, operations, and invocation-scoped Publisher capabilities.
Define concurrency, reentrancy, cancellation, and isolation requirements where applicable.
Define quiescence conditions including active operations, asynchronous work, reservations, and pending result custody.
Name the Recovery Owner and define how produced-but-unaccepted results are transferred and reconciled.
Define reuse/reset requirements and replacement identity behavior.
Define release confirmation and failed/indeterminate release reconciliation.
Define result detachment and historical provenance retention independently of Unit lifetime.
Define lifecycle behavior when the owning Step instance itself is quiesced or released.
specializationRequirements.completionRule: A concrete lifecycle specialization is complete when identity, readiness/admission, association eligibility, invocation/operation lifetime, Publisher interaction, quiescence, result custody, reuse, release, and historical provenance are explicit.

explicitNonGoals: No universal linear lifecycle state machine or mandatory lifecycle enum.
No mandatory object pool, factory, service locator, scheduler, reference counter, or global lifecycle manager.
No assumption that every Unit is permanently bound to one SPU.
No automatic release when the last Association ends or an invocation completes.
No release of accepted Publisher entries when the Unit is released.
No retention of runtime instances solely to preserve historical operation results.
No universal retry, replacement, fallback, or compensation policy.

references.relationship: Operation behavior, invocation, publication, custody, and provenance obligations.
Association validity, dissociation, and historical target provenance.
Detailed operation execution and reservation-backed result publication protocol.
Invocation-scoped publication capability and accepted-entry custody.
Step Composition lifecycle authority, supporting-unit coordination, and retained invocation evidence.
Independent Step-level ErrorHandlerResult integration and preservation.
Framework-level lifecycle coordination invariants refined by this specialized Lifecycle Contract; component-specific phases, resources, and custody remain authoritative.

frameworkCoordination.conformance: This contract specializes the shared Step Composition coordination invariants. Where the shared contract defines only conceptual identity roles or lifecycle distinctions, this document supplies the component-specific identity names, semantics, mechanics, and constraints.
frameworkCoordination.precedence: The common contract governs cross-cutting Step Composition coordination invariants. This specialized contract governs component-specific behavior and mechanics. Neither contract changes the component pattern?s distinct behavioral result semantics.
